note: No HSP90 inhibitor reached approval in breast cancer: HER2-positive xenografts predicted regressions that retaspimycin plus trastuzumab (0 of 26 responses) and single-agent ganetespib (2 of 13 HER2-positive, trial failed stage 1) did not deliver, the TNBC and ER-positive xenografts were contradicted by 0 TNBC responses and a negative randomised fulvestrant trial (PFS 3.7 vs 3.6 months), and the class's ocular toxicity was reproduced in rats only after the clinic had seen it.
label: Breast cancer (HSP90 inhibitors)

engagement.model: HER2-positive breast cancer xenografts (BT-474, JIMT-1) with HER2, p-AKT and HSP70 readouts
engagement.note: Luminespib in BT-474 xenografts: HSP90-p23 dissociation, ERBB2 and P-AKT loss and HSP70 induction tracked growth inhibition; no patient PD comparison yet.
engagement.short: HER2 loss and HSP70 rise in BT-474 xenografts
engagement.quote: Therapeutic effects were concordant with changes in pharmacodynamic markers, including HSP90-p23 dissociation, decreases in ERBB2 and P-AKT, and increased HSP70 protein levels.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. No NDA was ever filed for any member, so whether the model was filed is unknown.
engagement.judgement: Opens the track at the first member-drug HER2-positive breast xenograft paper (epub April 2008); Eccles 2008 (10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-07-5256) reports the same drug, model and markers the same month. The luminespib phase 1 (NCT00526045) had started in 2007 on data not then published.

engagement.model: HER2-positive breast cancer xenografts (BT-474, JIMT-1) with HER2, p-AKT and HSP70 readouts
engagement.note: Alvespimycin plus trastuzumab in 28 patients (25 breast): Hsp70 in peripheral blood lymphocytes rose through four weeks, most at 80-100 mg/m2; the xenografts' HSP70 readout moved.
engagement.short: HSP70 induced in breast patients' lymphocytes
engagement.quote: Hsp70 effect continued to increase across four weeks and was most pronounced at 80 and 100 mg/m(2).
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Population mostly HER2-positive breast (25 of 28); NCT00803556 has no posted results. Gaykema 2014 (10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-14-0491) gives the proximal readout with the model's own drug: on luminespib 70 mg/m2 the 89Zr-trastuzumab PET HER2 signal change was heterogeneous but tracked lesion size change (r2 0.69). Saif 2014 (10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-13-1257) gives BIIB021 Hsp70 rises above 150% and serum HER2-ECD falls above 15% in mixed solid tumours.
engagement.reason: HSP70 and HER2 readouts moved in patients
engagement.magnitude_basis: Hsp70 induction in peripheral blood lymphocytes, reported qualitatively
engagement.population: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (25 of 28 patients), phase 1 with trastuzumab
engagement.judgement: Scored same because the model's readouts moved in dosed breast patients, independent of the later efficacy misses. readout_tier is downstream because HSP70 is the heat-shock response, not HSP90's own client; the proximal readout (HER2 depletion on 89Zr-trastuzumab PET, Gaykema 2014) was heterogeneous, so I did not promote the tier. product_in_model is false because the HER2 xenograft papers dosed luminespib (Jensen, Eccles) and retaspimycin (Leow 2009) while the patient paper dosed alvespimycin; the pairing is mine.

engagement.model: HER2-overexpressing SKOV-3 xenograft with 89Zr-trastuzumab PET readout of luminespib-induced HER2 downregulation (Oude Munnink 2010)
engagement.note: Luminespib 50 mg/kg cut 89Zr-trastuzumab tumour uptake 41% on microPET in SKOV-3 xenografts, proposed as an early biomarker for HER2-positive breast patients; no patient comparison.
engagement.short: PET shows HER2 loss in xenografts
engagement.quote: NVP-AUY922 effectively downregulates HER2, which can be monitored and quantified in vivo non-invasively with 89Zr-trastuzumab PET.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The model is an ovarian HER2-amplified line (SKOV-3), chosen for HER2 level, and the paper names HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer as the target population, with the clinical evaluation already under way (NCT01081600 opened 2010-02). Epub 2009-12-24, print 2010.
engagement.population: SKOV-3 HER2-overexpressing ovarian xenografts in nude mice, luminespib 50 mg/kg every other day
engagement.judgement: Opens at the epub. A separate track from her2-breast-xenograft under this run's identity rule: a different tumour (SKOV-3, ovarian), a different readout (non-invasive HER2 PET rather than tumour western or IHC) and a different prediction (that PET-measured HER2 loss would read out luminespib's target engagement in patients). The draft's engagement #2 confidence note already mentions the patient result but books it under the BT-474 track.

engagement.model: HER2-overexpressing SKOV-3 xenograft with 89Zr-trastuzumab PET readout of luminespib-induced HER2 downregulation (Oude Munnink 2010)
engagement.note: Luminespib 70 mg/m2 weekly, 16 breast patients: 89Zr-trastuzumab PET HER2 signal fell 18% on average across 29 lesions, heterogeneous, and tracked CT size change.
engagement.short: HER2 PET change tracked CT response
engagement.quote: SUVmax change in individual tumor lesions on baseline versus 3 weeks 89Zr-trastuzumab PET was heterogeneous and related to size change on CT after 8 weeks treatment (r2 = 0.69; P = 0.006).
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (Firecrawl). 89Zr-trastuzumab PET was feasible in 6 of 10 HER2-positive patients, 5 with repeat scans, 29 lesions, average SUVmax decrease 18% (Figure 2 legend) against the model's 41% mean reduction; the introduction restates the xenograft result (radiolabeled trastuzumab uptake reduced on average 50% in breast xenografts on 17-AAG) but the discussion does not set model and patient numbers side by side, so comparison_stated is false. The ER-positive arm (89Zr-bevacizumab PET) did not correlate with CT response and is not this model's readout. Registry records NCT01081600 (PET, 7 enrolled) and NCT00526045 (treatment) have no posted results; the paper's epub date is not on PubMed, print 2014-08-01.
engagement.magnitude_basis: Mean reduction in 89Zr-trastuzumab tumour uptake after luminespib: 41% in SKOV-3 xenografts versus 18% average SUVmax decrease across 29 lesions in HER2-positive patients
engagement.population: HER2-positive (10) and ER-positive (6) metastatic breast cancer, luminespib 70 mg/m2 weekly; PET analysable in 6 HER2-positive patients
engagement.judgement: Same, partial: the model's readout (loss of 89Zr-trastuzumab PET signal after luminespib) moved in dosed HER2-positive breast patients and tracked lesion response, though heterogeneously and at under half the xenograft magnitude. Readout is proximal because HER2 is the chaperone's client, degraded directly on HSP90 inhibition, not a downstream biomarker. The pairing is between the Groningen group's own xenograft paper and its clinical follow-up with the same drug; the clinical paper restates the model result as rationale rather than comparing, so comparison_stated is false and model_src names the xenograft paper.

dose.model: HER2-positive breast cancer xenografts (BT-474, JIMT-1) with HER2, p-AKT and HSP70 readouts
dose.note: Weekly 30 mg/kg luminespib gave BT-474 tumours over 1,000 times the cellular GI50 for about two days and growth inhibition on once-weekly dosing; no human exposure comparison yet.
dose.short: Weekly regimen set from BT-474 exposure
dose.quote: Intravenous acute administration of NVP-AUY922 to athymic mice (30 mg/kg) bearing subcutaneous BT-474 breast tumors resulted in drug levels in excess of 1,000 times the cellular GI50 value for about 2 days.
dose.judgement: The model's regimen target was once-weekly dosing with multi-day tumour exposure far above GI50. Leow 2009 (10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-08-1038) adds that retaspimycin plus lapatinib was tolerated at 50 mg/kg, a tolerability statement but no NOAEL or MTD, so margin_stated stays null.

dose.model: NCI rat and beagle dog repeat-dose (daily x5 intravenous) toxicology of alvespimycin with plasma and tissue PK (Glaze 2005)
dose.note: Rat MTD 12 and dog MTD 8 mg/m2 per day, daily x5, with a phase 1 start of 1.3 mg/m2 per day; no human comparison.
dose.quote: The MTD of 17-DMAG was 12 mg/m2 per day in rats and 8 mg/m2 per day in dogs; therefore, the recommended starting dose for phase I trial is 1.3 mg/m2 per day for 5 days.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Springer, paywalled). An NCI Developmental Therapeutics Program package run before the first phase 1 (the abstract's 'recent approval of 17-DMAG for clinical use'); the run dates are not public, so the epub year (2005-06-29) is the proxy for first use. The package states tolerated doses, not an efficacious exposure.
dose.population: Rats and beagle dogs, daily x5 intravenous (one dog cohort oral)
dose.judgement: Opens the toxicology track at publication. margin_stated is true because the package states MTDs in both species and a starting dose, a tolerability margin in the sense of decision 16, even though no efficacious exposure is named alongside it. Its own track: a different system (GLP-style repeat-dose toxicology in two species) and a different prediction (tolerated dose and dose-limiting organs) from the HER2 xenograft dose track.

dose.model: NCI rat and beagle dog repeat-dose (daily x5 intravenous) toxicology of alvespimycin with plasma and tissue PK (Glaze 2005)
dose.note: Weekly alvespimycin escalated from 60 to 100 mg/m2, MTD 80 mg/m2: the dog-derived start was conservative and the dog's dose-limiting harms never limited dosing.
dose.short: Human MTD 80 mg/m2 weekly, dog margin held
dose.quote: The recommended dose of alvespimycin for further study in this combination is 80 mg/m(2) weekly.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The model stated tolerated doses but no efficacious exposure, so only the tolerability half of the dose question is answered: alvespimycin never reached an efficacy test in breast cancer (NCT00780000, monotherapy in HER2-positive breast, terminated after 4 patients, no results), so whether the reached dose was enough is unknown. The phase 1 started at 60 mg/m2 weekly, far above the 1.3 mg/m2 x5 start proposed from the dog, on earlier monotherapy phase 1 data in mixed solid tumours (not scored here). NCT00803556 has no posted results. Magnitude is computed per course (dog MTD 8 mg/m2 x5 = 40 mg/m2 versus human 80 mg/m2 per week); per administration the human MTD was 10x the dog MTD.
dose.reason: Stated MTD margin held in patients
dose.magnitude_basis: Tolerated dose per course: dog MTD 8 mg/m2 per day x5 (40 mg/m2) versus human MTD 80 mg/m2 once weekly with trastuzumab
dose.population: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (25 of 28 patients), phase 1 with trastuzumab, weekly 60-100 mg/m2
dose.judgement: Same under decision 16: the model stated an MTD and the dog's dose-limiting harms (GI, renal, gallbladder, marrow) did not stop escalation to or above that exposure; the DLTs that set the human MTD (keratitis, LV dysfunction) were unpredicted and are counted once, in safety. The 'enough' half is unanswerable because no efficacy trial followed, so a stricter reader could hold this at untested; scored because the margin was stated and held. The pairing is mine (Jhaveri 2012 does not cite the toxicology paper in its abstract).

efficacy.model: HER2-positive breast cancer xenografts (BT-474, JIMT-1) with HER2, p-AKT and HSP70 readouts
efficacy.note: Daily luminespib gave BT474 treated/control 21% with ERBB2 depletion; Jensen 2008 and Leow 2009 (retaspimycin, with trastuzumab) made HER2-positive breast the named indication.
efficacy.short: BT474 xenografts: growth inhibition, HER2 depleted
efficacy.quote: This produced statistically significant growth inhibition and/or regressions in human tumor xenografts with diverse oncogenic profiles: BT474 breast tumor treated/control, 21%; A2780 ovarian, 11%; U87MG glioblastoma, 7%; PC3 prostate, 37%; and WM266.4 melanoma, 31%.
efficacy.judgement: The track pools the members' HER2-positive breast xenograft work as one system: Jensen 2008 (10.1186/bcr1996, BT-474, luminespib), Leow 2009 (10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-08-1038, retaspimycin alone and with trastuzumab or lapatinib, including trastuzumab-resistant JIMT-1), Scaltriti 2011 (10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-10-0966, retaspimycin in trastuzumab-resistant xenografts) and Friedland 2014 (10.1007/s10637-013-9971-6, ganetespib regression of BT-474). Tanespimycin's HER2-positive work is not a member's and is set aside.

efficacy.model: HER2-positive breast cancer xenografts (BT-474, JIMT-1) with HER2, p-AKT and HSP70 readouts
efficacy.note: Retaspimycin plus trastuzumab in 26 trastuzumab-pretreated HER2-positive patients: no confirmed responses, 62% stable disease, Simon stage 1 not passed; the xenograft combination regressions did not transfer. Design: single-arm combination with trastuzumab, Simon two-stage on response rate, scored on its primary endpoint.
efficacy.quote: Modest clinical activity was observed, but did not meet criteria for trial expansion.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The registry says the trial was terminated for 'limited efficacy response observed during interim analysis'; no results posted. Later HER2-positive data do not reverse the track: luminespib plus trastuzumab 22% response in 41 trastuzumab-progressed patients (Kong 2016) with no stated target rate, ganetespib monotherapy 2 of 13 (Jhaveri 2014) in a trial that failed its Simon stage 1, and the alvespimycin HER2-positive phase 2 (NCT00780000) terminated after 4 patients without results.
efficacy.reason: Xenograft regressions; no responses in HER2+ patients
efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft growth delay and regressions with trastuzumab versus 0 of 26 confirmed responses

patient_trials.quote: The ORR in this unselected population was 9%, with all responses coming from the subset of patients with HER2-positive MBC (2/13; 15%).
Of the 41 patients in the 70 mg/m2 cohort, the overall response rate (complete or partial responses) was 22.0% and 48.8% patients had stable disease.
The overall response rate was 22% (2/9 patients had partial response) and stable disease was seen in 56% (5/9 patients).

efficacy.judgement: Contra rather than partial-same: the model's specific prediction, that retaspimycin plus trastuzumab regresses trastuzumab-resistant HER2-positive tumours (Leow 2009, JIMT-1), was tested in exactly that population and gave no confirmed responses. One drug's contra beats another's same on the track, so Kong 2016 (luminespib, 22%) and the 2 of 13 ganetespib responses sit in patient_trials without changing status. Jhaveri 2012 (alvespimycin plus trastuzumab phase 1, 1 PR and 7 SD in HER2-positive breast) has a DLT primary endpoint and is not scored for efficacy. Modi attributes the miss to possible underdosing, hence source_calls_it unresolved.

efficacy.model: Triple-negative breast cancer xenografts (MDA-MB-231 and others; orthotopic and metastasis readouts)
efficacy.note: Alvespimycin 75 mg/kg in MDA-MB-231 xenografts: drug retained in tumour at 48 h with Raf-1 about 20% lower; a PK/PD model, no efficacy claim or patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: Raf-1 in tumors of 17DMAG-treated mice killed at 4, 7, 24 and 48 h was about 20% lower than in tumors from vehicle-treated mice.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the track at the first member-drug use of a TNBC xenograft. The efficacy prediction came later from ganetespib: Friedland 2014 (10.1007/s10637-013-9971-6, MDA-MB-231 growth suppression), Proia 2014 (10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-13-2166, TNBC xenografts, lung metastases suppressed, chemotherapy combinations) and Xiang 2014 (10.1007/s00109-013-1102-5, orthotopic MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-435 growth and metastasis blocked). Own track, not the HER2 system: different lines, HIF-1 and multi-client dependence rather than HER2 degradation, and a different prediction.

efficacy.model: Triple-negative breast cancer xenografts (MDA-MB-231 and others; orthotopic and metastasis readouts)
efficacy.note: Single-agent ganetespib in 22 unselected metastatic patients failed its Simon stage 1 (ORR 9%); no RECIST response in TNBC, one TNBC patient with lung-metastasis regression. Design: single-arm Simon two-stage with a preset response bar; scored on the TNBC patients within it.
efficacy.short: No TNBC responders; trial failed stage 1
efficacy.quote: The study did not meet the prespecified criteria for ORR in the first stage of the Simon 2-stage model in this heavily pretreated unselected population of MBC.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the TNBC subgroup size is not in the abstract and the primary endpoint was over the unselected 22, so the TNBC call rests on 0 RECIST responses in that subset. Proia 2014 (Synta) pairs the model with 'marked tumor shrinkage of metastatic lung and lymphatic lesions' in TNBC patients, case-level, not an endpoint. ENCHANT-1 (NCT01677455, first-line ganetespib in HER2-positive or TNBC, primary ORR, 51 patients) completed with no posted results and no paper I could find, so its TNBC cohort is unverified; the ganetespib plus paclitaxel TNBC pilot (NCT02637375) never opened. Year is the epub (2013-12-28); registry results posted 2015-11-20.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft growth and metastasis suppression versus 0 RECIST responses in TNBC

patient_trials.quote: One patient with TNBC had objective tumor regression in the lung metastases.

efficacy.population: Triple-negative metastatic breast cancer subset of an unselected phase 2
efficacy.judgement: Contra on the primary endpoint under decision 13: the data showed no TNBC response by RECIST and a failed stage 1, whatever the sponsor's model paper said about regressions; Jhaveri calls the TNBC signal 'activity', hence source_calls_it partial. A stricter reader could hold this at untested because the subset is small and its size unreported; I scored it because the model's own sponsor used these same patients as its clinical evidence (Proia 2014).

efficacy.model: Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer xenograft (MCF-7, ganetespib monotherapy)
efficacy.note: Ganetespib suppressed MCF-7 xenograft growth and destabilised ER-pathway clients; no fulvestrant combination modelled, no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: This multimodal activity translated to potent antitumor efficacy in vivo, suppressing tumor growth in MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 xenografts and inducing tumor regression in the BT-474 model.
efficacy.judgement: Own track: a different line and a different prediction (ER-dependent tumours respond because ER is an HSP90 client) from the HER2 and TNBC systems. The fulvestrant trial (NCT01560416) started June 2012, before this paper; the abstract does not state a fulvestrant combination in mice.

efficacy.model: Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer xenograft (MCF-7, ganetespib monotherapy)
efficacy.note: Randomised phase 2, fulvestrant with or without ganetespib in 50 endocrine-resistant HR-positive patients: median PFS 3.7 vs 3.6 months, diarrhoea 97% vs 7%; primary endpoint missed. Design: randomised fulvestrant plus ganetespib versus fulvestrant alone; combination scored on its primary endpoint, PFS.
efficacy.quote: Median PFS was similar between arms (3.7 vs 3.6 months; log-rank P = .79).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the paper (Grinshpun 2026, The Oncologist, PMID 42873573) is epub 2026 and the registry results posting (2019-01-03) sets the year. The trial paper says ganetespib had 'demonstrated anti-tumor activity in preclinical breast cancer models' without naming the model, so the pairing to Friedland 2014 is mine. BIIB021 plus exemestane in HR-positive metastatic breast cancer (NCT01004081, phase 2, 54 patients, completed) has no posted results and no paper I could find.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: MCF-7 xenograft growth suppression versus median PFS 3.7 vs 3.6 months (log-rank P = .79)

patient_trials.quote: Adding ganetespib to fulvestrant did not improve clinical outcomes and increased toxicity

efficacy.population: Hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, endocrine-resistant metastatic breast cancer
efficacy.judgement: Contra: the model predicted ER-positive tumours respond to ganetespib and the only randomised test of the class in breast cancer showed no PFS gain. The model never tested the fulvestrant combination, so a stricter reader could say the trial asked a question the model did not; I scored it because the trial's rationale is the model's (ER is an HSP90 client) and single-agent HR-positive activity was never shown either (Jhaveri 2014: all responses HER2-positive).

efficacy.model: ER-positive human breast cancer xenografts on hormone antagonists with sub-growth-inhibitory ganetespib, resistance-emergence readout (Whitesell 2014)
efficacy.note: Sub-growth-inhibitory ganetespib with hormone antagonists delayed resistance emergence in ER-positive xenografts, no activity alone; the only trial (established resistance) tested a different question.
efficacy.short: Low-dose ganetespib delays endocrine resistance in mice
efficacy.quote: had no overt anticancer activity on its own, it dramatically impaired the emergence of resistance to hormone antagonists both in cell culture and in mice.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for the model (PMC4280614 is open access; not read in full). Grinshpun 2026 (PMID 42873573, PMC13728916, full text) names this model as the fulvestrant trial's direct preclinical rationale and itself states that the trial population (established endocrine resistance, ganetespib 150 mg/m2) differs from the model's question (delaying emergence in previously sensitive tumours at a sub-growth-inhibitory dose), so no admissible comparison exists. The trial's null (PFS 3.7 vs 3.6 months) is consistent with the model's 'no overt anticancer activity on its own' but does not test it. Synta's D.A. Proia is a co-author of the model paper.
efficacy.reason: Emergence prediction never tested in patients
efficacy.population: ER-positive human breast cancer xenografts in mice on hormone antagonists, with or without low-dose ganetespib

patient_trials.quote: the preclinical data supporting the combination of endocrine therapy with ganetespib were derived from a model in which it delayed the emergence of endocrine resistance in previously sensitive tumors, rather than a model of reversing resistance once established.

efficacy.judgement: Untested, not contra: the trial that cites this model as rationale (Grinshpun 2026, NCT01560416) tested established resistance at full dose, and says so, while the model predicted delayed emergence in sensitive tumours at a sub-growth-inhibitory dose; the trial is recorded in patient_trials because it changes no status. Its own track, separate from er-breast-xenograft (Friedland 2014: full-dose monotherapy growth inhibition), because the regimen, readout and prediction differ. A prospective test would need an endocrine-sensitive population with time to resistance as endpoint; none was run (BIIB021 plus exemestane, NCT01004081, has no results).

efficacy.model: HER2-positive breast cancer xenografts (BT-474, JIMT-1) with HER2, p-AKT and HSP70 readouts
efficacy.note: Retaspimycin (IPI-504) with trastuzumab gave more tumour growth delay than either drug in HER2-positive xenografts, including trastuzumab-resistant JIMT-1; no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.short: Retaspimycin plus trastuzumab beat either alone
efficacy.quote: Although, as expected, trastuzumab alone did not exhibit any significant antitumor activity in the trastuzumab-resistant JIMT-1 model, IPI-504 administered in combination with trastuzumab yielded greater antitumor efficacy than either agent alone.
efficacy.judgement: Opener for the retaspimycin track at the model's first use with that drug; this is the prediction efficacy 2 (Modi 2013) tested.

efficacy.model: Triple-negative breast cancer xenografts (MDA-MB-231 and others; orthotopic and metastasis readouts)
efficacy.note: Ganetespib suppressed MDA-MB-231 (triple-negative) xenograft growth; first ganetespib use of the TNBC system, no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: This multimodal activity translated to potent antitumor efficacy in vivo, suppressing tumor growth in MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 xenografts and inducing tumor regression in the BT-474 model.
efficacy.judgement: Opener for the ganetespib track of the TNBC xenograft system at its first ganetespib use (Friedland 2014, epub May 2013); efficacy 4 is the later entry.

safety.model: Mouse xenograft studies with cardiac and liver readouts (ganetespib)
safety.note: Ganetespib's preclinical profile claimed no cardiac or liver toxicity, the geldanamycin liabilities; no breast-cancer patient comparison yet.
safety.short: Mice: no cardiac or liver toxicity claimed
safety.quote: Importantly, ganetespib showed no evidence of cardiac or liver toxicity.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; epub December 2011, print 2012. No GLP toxicology for any member is public (no NDA).
safety.judgement: The only public animal-safety statement for a member; it is an efficacy paper's claim, not a toxicology package.

safety.model: Mouse xenograft studies with cardiac and liver readouts (ganetespib)
safety.note: Ganetespib in 22 breast patients: diarrhoea, fatigue, nausea and hypersensitivity, no cardiac or hepatic signal; the stated prediction held, but the mice were silent on the GI toxicity that dominated. Ruling: a passing no-toxicity claim in an efficacy paper is a scored safety prediction; it named no cardiac or liver harm and none appeared, so it stays matched.
safety.short: No cardiac or liver signal; GI unpredicted
safety.quote: Most common toxicities, largely grade 1/2, were diarrhea, fatigue, nausea, and hypersensitivity reaction.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; 22 patients. The randomised fulvestrant trial (10.1093/oncolo/oyag414) later put ganetespib diarrhoea at 97% vs 7%, a harm a mouse could have shown. Year is the epub (2013-12-28); registry results posted 2015-11-20.
safety.reason: No cardiac or liver signal; GI unpredicted
safety.magnitude_basis: absence of a cardiac or hepatic adverse-event signal
safety.population: Unselected metastatic breast cancer, ganetespib monotherapy
safety.judgement: Scored on the stated prediction (no cardiac or liver toxicity), which held in breast patients; a stricter reading scores the mouse silence on diarrhoea, the class's dominant harm (97% in the randomised trial), as contra. The alvespimycin cardiac DLT (Jhaveri 2012, grade III left ventricular dysfunction with trastuzumab) and Modi 2013's single grade 3 transaminase rise belong to other members with no public animal safety statement, so they are not scored against this ganetespib track.

safety.model: Rat retinal damage model (photoreceptor histology, retinal Hsp70, retina/plasma exposure)
safety.note: Built after luminespib's visual disorders were known in patients: in rats it killed photoreceptors and stayed in retina, reproducing the known harm. Split by drug: alvespimycin and ganetespib are their own tracks.
safety.short: Rat retina reproduced the ocular-toxicity split
safety.quote: Both 17-DMAG and NVP-AUY922 induced strong yet restricted retinal Hsp70 up-regulation and promoted marked photoreceptor cell death 24h after the final dose.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; Synta (ganetespib's sponsor) authored the model. Breast-patient data: Jhaveri 2012 alvespimycin plus trastuzumab, reversible grade III keratitis in 2 patients plus blurry vision and dry eyes; Kong 2016 luminespib plus trastuzumab, ocular events in 91.1% with 4.4% discontinuing; Jhaveri 2014 lists no ocular event among ganetespib's common toxicities.
safety.magnitude_basis: photoreceptor death and retinal retention versus clinical visual-disorder incidence, by drug
safety.population: Luminespib-treated patients with visual disorders known before the model; breast data in Kong 2016
safety.judgement: A retrodiction by the paper's own framing ('In human trials certain Hsp90 inhibitors, including 17-DMAG and NVP-AUY922, have caused visual disorders ... others such as 17-AAG and ganetespib have not'), so retro, never same. Kong 2016's 91% ocular events on luminespib came after the model but confirm a harm already known, not a fresh prediction, so no new entry. Whether sponsor toxicology flagged retinal toxicity before the alvespimycin or luminespib phase 1 trials is not public (no NDA), so no contra is scored against a toxicology track for the ocular miss.

safety.model: NCI rat and beagle dog repeat-dose (daily x5 intravenous) toxicology of alvespimycin with plasma and tissue PK (Glaze 2005)
safety.note: Alvespimycin daily x5: GI, marrow and hepatic toxicity in rats and dogs, renal and gallbladder in dogs; silent on heart and eye; no patient comparison.
safety.short: Rat/dog: GI, marrow, liver, renal, gallbladder
safety.quote: Gastrointestinal and bone marrow toxicity were dose-limiting in rats, and gastrointestinal, renal, gallbladder and bone marrow toxicity were dose-limiting in dogs.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Springer, paywalled). The abstract lists the organ toxicities found and states all were reversible; it names no cardiac or ocular finding. Whether ophthalmic examination and ECG were part of the dog protocol is not in the abstract, but both are standard in a dog repeat-dose study, so silence on those organs is scorable.
safety.population: Rats and beagle dogs, daily x5 intravenous (one dog cohort oral)
safety.judgement: Opens the only prospective animal safety package published for a member drug. A separate track from ganetespib-mouse-tox (different drug, species and stated predictions) and from the rat-retina model (a retrodiction built after the clinic saw visual disorders).

safety.model: NCI rat and beagle dog repeat-dose (daily x5 intravenous) toxicology of alvespimycin with plasma and tissue PK (Glaze 2005)
safety.note: Alvespimycin plus trastuzumab in breast patients: DLTs were LV dysfunction and keratitis, unstated by the model; predicted renal and gallbladder harms never appeared; diarrhoea held.
safety.short: Keratitis and heart DLTs unpredicted; renal never seen
safety.quote: Dose-limiting toxicities (DLT) were: grade III left ventricular systolic dysfunction presenting as congestive heart failure in 1 patient (100 mg/m(2)), and reversible grade III keratitis in two patients (80 mg/m(2)).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The cardiac DLT occurred on trastuzumab, which has its own LV toxicity, so attribution to alvespimycin is uncertain; keratitis is not confounded (blurry vision and dry eyes were also common) and ophthalmic examination is standard in dog toxicology. Marrow and hepatic toxicity, predicted in both species, are not reported in the abstract; diarrhoea (common, one grade 3) is the GI prediction that held. NCT00803556 has no posted results. Alvespimycin monotherapy phase 1 trials were in mixed solid tumours and are not scored on this breast tile.
safety.reason: Silent on keratitis, heart; renal never came

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; Synta (ganetespib's sponsor) authored the model. Breast-patient data: Jhaveri 2012 alvespimycin plus trastuzumab, reversible grade III keratitis in 2 patients plus blurry vision and dry eyes; Kong 2016 luminespib plus trastuzumab, ocular events in 91.1% with 4.4% discontinuing; Jhaveri 2014 lists no ocular event among ganetespib's common toxicities.
safety.magnitude_basis: photoreceptor death and retinal retention versus clinical visual-disorder incidence, by drug
safety.population: Alvespimycin-treated patients with visual disorders known before the model; breast data in Jhaveri 2012
safety.judgement: A retrodiction by the paper's own framing ('In human trials certain Hsp90 inhibitors, including 17-DMAG and NVP-AUY922, have caused visual disorders ... others such as 17-AAG and ganetespib have not'), so retro, never same. Kong 2016's 91% ocular events on luminespib came after the model but confirm a harm already known, not a fresh prediction, so no new entry. Whether sponsor toxicology flagged retinal toxicity before the alvespimycin or luminespib phase 1 trials is not public (no NDA), so no contra is scored against a toxicology track for the ocular miss.
